sources.citation: game-design: a round nonmetallic (PVC) ceiling box of 4 in outside diameter for a luminaire, a common class listed to UL 514C and described by NEMA OS 2 (cited by number). Outside taken as a cylinder of 102 mm diameter and 57 mm deep (4 in and 2-1/4 in), with 3 mm drawn walls, so the inside is 96 mm across and 54 mm deep; its bounding box is 102 × 102 × 57 mm. Unverified against a specific manufacturer drawing; electrical-realism-reviewer checked the class dimensions (2026-11-12).

game-design: computed from the inside dimensions above as a plain cylinder, π × (96 / 2)² × 54 = 390864 mm³ (about 23.85 in³), rounded to a whole mm³: about 17.5 % above the volume round nonmetallic boxes of this class are marked with, because their walls taper. It is the drawn box's geometric volume, not a marked volume and not from any code table, and it must not be used unchanged as the box-fill allowance (P4 decides between a marked-volume field and a stated rule).

game-design: four built-in cable clamps (knock-in tabs) a quarter-turn apart around the wall, one cable each, the box clamps the cable itself. No mount for a luminaire in P3 (P4 brings luminaires). Positions are on the round wall at its quarter points and are not taken from a product drawing.
game-design: nailed to the side of a joist or stud through its bracket (studFlange, common practice); it takes its full width along the framing member.
